distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer disease leaf for systemic small-vessel IgA-dominant immune-complex vasculitis involving skin, joints, gastrointestinal tract, and kidney. The leaf is independent of age, trigger, renal severity, gastrointestinal severity, biopsy site, recurrence status, and treatment response.
distillation_scope.boundary_policy: IgA nephropathy without systemic vasculitis, ANCA-associated vasculitis, cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis without IgA-dominant systemic pattern, meningococcemia, DIC, thrombocytopenic purpura, SLE flare, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, PAN, drug eruption, erysipelas/cellulitis, infectious endocarditis, IBD, appendicitis, intussusception from a structural lead point, and generic sepsis remain competing manifolds or triggers/context. They are not appended to the disease name.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking should use non-thrombocytopenic palpable purpura, dependent lower-extremity or buttock distribution, arthralgia or arthritis, abdominal pain, vomiting or diarrhea, GI bleeding, imaging or endoscopic bowel edema/ulceration, hematuria, proteinuria, creatinine/eGFR, blood pressure, inflammatory markers, complement and IgA context when measured, and biopsy only when testing post-workup mode. Trigger, organism, vaccine, drug, adult/pediatric status, renal severity, and GI complication type are axes or risk/treatment context rather than disease-name qualifiers.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Mucosal, infectious, vaccine, drug, or environmental trigger activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Upper respiratory or gastrointestinal infection, vaccine exposure, medication exposure, malignancy context, or other antigenic stimulation can precede IgA vasculitis by days to weeks.
Aberrantly glycosylated IgA1 and anti-glycan antibodies form circulating immune complexes that deposit in small vessels and glomerular mesangium.

IgA-dominant immune-complex deposition activates alternative/lectin complement, neutrophil recruitment, leukocytoclasis, fibrinoid injury, and vascular leak in dermal, gut, joint, and renal microvessels.
Postcapillary venule vasculitis in dependent skin produces non-thrombocytopenic palpable purpura, petechiae, edema, and occasionally bullous or necrotic lesions.
Sterile periarticular edema, tenosynovial inflammation, and transient arthritis or arthralgia affect ankles, knees, wrists, elbows, hands, or feet, usually non-erosive.
Small-vessel vasculitis in bowel wall causes submucosal edema, capillary hemorrhage, erosions, ulcers, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, occult blood, hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Severe GI ischemia, obstruction, intussusception, and perforation activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Marked bowel edema, intramural hemorrhage, mesenteric vasculitis, dysmotility, hematoma, or ischemia can generate intussusception, obstruction, necrosis, perforation, peritonitis, hemorrhagic shock, or need for surgery.
Mesangial IgA-dominant immune-complex deposition with endocapillary proliferation, hematuria, proteinuria, and sometimes crescents or rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
Persistent proteinuria, crescents, glomerulosclerosis, tubulointerstitial scarring, hypertension, and reduced GFR determine long-term CKD and kidney failure risk after active nephritis.
IL-6 and innate immune activation produce fever, leukocytosis or neutrophilia, thrombocytosis, elevated CRP/ESR, hypoalbuminemia, and constitutional symptoms.
High-dose glucocorticoids and steroid-sparing immunosuppressants can reduce vasculitis activity but add infection, cytopenia, metabolic, fertility, renal, hepatic, and GI toxicity contexts.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Only when purpura is present; distribution should not be consumed without parent purpura.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Lower-extremity distribution is a satellite of the main purpura finding.
Bowel edema and irritation drive both pain and vomiting.
More severe mucosal vasculitis can produce both pain and bleeding.
Obstruction or ischemia can produce peritoneal signs.
Intussusception can compromise mesenteric blood flow.
Ischemic necrosis can progress to perforation.
GI bleeding is a major component of aggregate bleeding risk.
Active sediment includes hematuria and casts.
Persistent heavy proteinuria predicts CKD progression.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Rising creatinine or reduced urine output

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Renal impairment changes treatment dosing and toxicity.
Bleeding can cause shock and death.
Perforation is one of the major acute mortality drivers.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Bleeding requires closer hemodynamic and hemoglobin monitoring.
Renal involvement requires serial urinalysis, creatinine, BP, and proteinuria follow-up.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supportive vector for mild or resolving cutaneous/articular/GI symptoms and for physiologic stabilization while organ-risk axes are assessed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal disease or GI bleeding makes NSAID toxicity dominate symptom benefit.
NSAIDs can worsen AKI and reduce renal perfusion.
NSAIDs can aggravate mucosal bleeding.

side_effects.interpretation: NSAID renal hemodynamic toxicity, especially with nephritis, dehydration, CKD, ACEi/ARB, or diuretics.
NSAIDs can aggravate GI mucosal bleeding.

treatments.context_specific_role: Pain-control vector only when renal and GI bleeding risk is low.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroids often shorten severe inflammatory abdominal pain.
Renal disease increases rationale for anti-inflammatory renal trajectory control and close follow-up.
Active serious infection can be worsened by systemic steroids.

side_effects.interpretation: Infection risk rises with dose and duration.
Symptoms of ischemia/perforation can be masked during steroid treatment.

treatments.context_specific_role: Systemic anti-inflammatory vector for significant abdominal, cutaneous, articular, or renal involvement.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe GI vasculitis may require rapid inflammatory suppression.
Crescentic nephritis is organ-threatening.
Pulse steroids can worsen infection.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapid suppression vector for organ-threatening GI or renal IgAV when severe inflammatory activity dominates.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Persistent nephritis/proteinuria increases need for steroid-sparing renal control.
Refractory GI vasculitis has case-report support for MMF.
MMF is teratogenic.

treatments.context_specific_role: Steroid-sparing or refractory-control vector for persistent nephritis or refractory GI involvement.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Persistent renal inflammatory activity may need steroid-sparing maintenance.
Cytopenia increases toxicity risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Steroid-sparing or maintenance immunosuppression vector in selected persistent/recurrent disease.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Crescentic or rapidly progressive nephritis is the context where cytotoxic suppression may be considered.
Cyclophosphamide is gonadotoxic and teratogenic.

treatments.context_specific_role: High-toxicity vector for selected organ-threatening renal or refractory systemic IgAV when benefit outweighs toxicity.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Refractory adult IgAV nephritis or systemic disease has case-series support for B-cell depletion.
Active serious infection increases risk from B-cell depletion.

side_effects.interpretation: B-cell depletion and hypogammaglobulinemia increase infection risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Refractory, relapsing, or steroid-sparing B-cell depletion vector in selected adult IgAV contexts.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal replacement is a support vector for severe AKI complications, not a direct vasculitis treatment.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Classic dependent purpura is common in children.
Intussusception is more common in pediatric GI IgAV than in adults.

age_3_to_15.trajectory_modulation: Higher prior and often self-limited course, but renal and GI hazards still need surveillance.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Adult IgAV has more frequent and severe renal involvement.
Adults more often present with AKI or impaired renal function.

adult_onset.trajectory_modulation: Lower incidence than childhood disease but higher renal, GI, treatment, and mortality risk.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Mucosal infection is a common antecedent trigger.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises prior and can amplify acute inflammatory markers.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Vaccines and drugs are reported triggers but do not define the disease leaf.

present.trajectory_modulation: May time-lock onset but should not restrict the disease manifold to a trigger subtype.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Hematuria and proteinuria identify renal IgAV activity.

hematuria_or_proteinuria_present.trajectory_modulation: Raises need for renal monitoring, BP/proteinuria control, and escalation when severe.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Nephrotic-range proteinuria defines high-risk renal phenotype.
Crescents identify rapidly progressive nephritic risk.
Severe renal pathology can require dialysis.

present.trajectory_modulation: Shifts renal trajectory toward organ-threatening disease and slower recovery.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Bleeding, obstruction, and peritonitis indicate severe bowel-wall disease.

Severe GI complications are major acute mortality drivers.

gi_bleeding_obstruction_intussusception_.trajectory_modulation: Raises surgical, ICU, transfusion, and rapid immunosuppression decision stakes.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Background kidney disease raises baseline creatinine and lowers reserve.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises complication risk and changes treatment toxicity.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Active infection changes safety of steroids and immunosuppression.
Immunosuppression increases infection hazard.
Preexisting immunosuppression can alter WBC response.

present.trajectory_modulation: Increases toxicity of immunosuppressive vectors and raises mimic context.

supportive_care: Document purpura morphology, palpability, blanching, symmetry, dependent distribution, buttock/trunk/upper-extremity spread, edema, bullae, necrosis, and platelet count so thrombocytopenic purpura and infectious mimics are not conflated with IgAV.

Trend abdominal pain quality, vomiting, diarrhea, hematemesis, melena, hematochezia, stool occult blood, hemoglobin, lactate, peritoneal signs, and hemodynamics; image promptly when obstruction, intussusception, ischemia, or perforation is possible.

Trend urinalysis with sediment, urine protein quantification, serum creatinine, eGFR, albumin, potassium, and blood pressure at presentation and during follow-up; persistent proteinuria or rising creatinine should not be treated as a purely cutaneous flare.

Use skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence or renal biopsy when diagnosis or renal severity is uncertain; biopsy evidence is confirmatory/post-workup context unless the test mode explicitly includes diagnostic-workup information.

Preserve mimic evidence: ANCA, ANA/dsDNA, complements, cryoglobulins, hepatitis/HIV, blood cultures, stool studies, endocarditis evaluation, platelet count, coagulation, and imaging source evidence can all redirect ranking when truly present.
Avoid NSAIDs when renal involvement, dehydration, GI bleeding, peptic injury, anticoagulation, or high frailty risk is present; use renal-safe analgesia and antiemetics when needed.
During glucocorticoid therapy, monitor for masked surgical abdomen, GI perforation, infection, glucose elevation, blood pressure, fluid retention, and bone/GI protection needs.

For severe GI bleeding, obstruction, intussusception, ischemia, or perforation, coordinate gastroenterology, surgery, interventional radiology, ICU, transfusion support, and immunosuppression decisions rather than relying on immunosuppression alone.
For significant nephritis, coordinate nephrology and rheumatology; consider renal biopsy severity, proteinuria persistence, BP/proteinuria control, and renal replacement indications as separate axes.
Vaccination/infection/drug triggers should be retained as context but should not narrow the first-layer disease name; future subtype modeling can occur after the base IgAV manifold is diagnosed.

Do not force IgAV to win by deleting evidence for mimics such as ANCA vasculitis, SLE, cryoglobulinemia, thrombocytopenic purpura, meningococcemia, infective endocarditis, IBD, appendicitis, or structural intussusception.
